title: Derived exchange commutes around a commutative cube
statement:
Let $X_0,Y_0,S_0,T_0,X_1,Y_1,S_1,T_1$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $h_b:Y_b\to X_b$, $e_b:Y_b\to T_b$, $f_b:X_b\to S_b$, $g_b:T_b\to S_b$ for $b=0,1$, satisfying $f_bh_b=g_be_b$. Give morphisms $x:X_1\to X_0$, $y:Y_1\to Y_0$, $s:S_1\to S_0$, $a:T_1\to T_0$ satisfying $f_0x=sf_1$, $g_0a=sg_1$, $h_0y=xh_1$, and $e_0y=ae_1$.
On the bounded below derived categories $\Dplus(Z_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use derived inverse images and direct images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every commutative face, exchange means the canonical adjunction mate of its inverse-image comparison [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange]. Write $E_b:f_b^{-1}Rg_{b,*}\to Rh_{b,*}e_b^{-1}$ for the two square exchanges, $P:s^{-1}Rg_{0,*}\to Rg_{1,*}a^{-1}$ and $Q:x^{-1}Rh_{0,*}\to Rh_{1,*}y^{-1}$ for the comparison-face exchanges. For every $K\in\Dplus((T_0)_{\Et})$, under the canonical inverse-image composition identifications [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition],
$$ E_1(a^{-1}K)\circ f_1^{-1}P(K)=Q(e_0^{-1}K)\circ x^{-1}E_0(K). $$
Both sides are morphisms from $x^{-1}f_0^{-1}Rg_{0,*}K$ to $Rh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}a^{-1}K$, where the right side includes the identification $y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\cong e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$. No face is required to be cartesian and no exchange map is assumed invertible.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, the two-square exchange composition; Tag 07A7, remark-base-change. Agent-extracted cube comparison needed in the canonical-map verification in Tag 0EZT.

proof.text: By [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange], each of $E_0$, $E_1$, $P$ and $Q$ is the mate of its displayed inverse-image comparison. In the orientation of that definition, $E_b$ is the mate of $\theta_b:h_b^{-1}f_b^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_b^{-1}g_b^{-1}$, $P$ is the mate of $\theta_P:g_1^{-1}s^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}a^{-1}g_0^{-1}$, and $Q$ is the mate of $\theta_Q:h_1^{-1}x^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}y^{-1}h_0^{-1}$. These comparisons are defined for arbitrary commutative faces, so no cartesian or invertibility hypothesis has been introduced.

Paste the inverse-image comparisons in the two possible orders. The composite corresponding to the left-hand side is $\gamma=(e_1^{-1}\theta_P)\circ(\theta_1\,s^{-1})$, from $h_1^{-1}f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ to $e_1^{-1}a^{-1}g_0^{-1}$. The composite corresponding to the right-hand side is $\gamma'=(y^{-1}\theta_0)\circ(\theta_Q\,f_0^{-1})$, from $h_1^{-1}x^{-1}f_0^{-1}$ to $y^{-1}e_0^{-1}g_0^{-1}$. Let $\sigma:x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ be $(c^D_{s,f_1})^{-1}$ composed with transport along $f_0x=sf_1$ and with $c^D_{f_0,x}$, and let $\tau:y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$ be defined in the same way from $e_0y=ae_1$. Each of $\gamma\circ(h_1^{-1}\sigma)$ and $(\tau\,g_0^{-1})\circ\gamma'$ is a composite of whiskered isomorphisms $c^D$, their inverses and transports along the cube equations. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], the derived composition isomorphisms satisfy the associativity and unit identities. Hence both composites equal the transformation $h_1^{-1}x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\to(f_0xh_1)^{-1}=(g_0ae_1)^{-1}\to e_1^{-1}a^{-1}g_0^{-1}$ obtained from the triple composition isomorphisms, so $\gamma\circ(h_1^{-1}\sigma)=(\tau\,g_0^{-1})\circ\gamma'$.

Apply the mate-pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause 1, to the two pastings, with the adjunctions for $h_1$ and $g_0$ on the outside. The mate of $\gamma$ is $E_1(a^{-1}K)\circ f_1^{-1}P(K)$ and the mate of $\gamma'$ is $Q(e_0^{-1}K)\circ x^{-1}E_0(K)$. By the explicit unit-counit formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], mates are compatible with whiskering the two side functors by natural transformations. For $\sigma$ this uses naturality of the unit $\eta_{h_1}$, and for $\tau$ it uses naturality of $\tau$ against the counit $\varepsilon_{g_0}$. So the mate of $\gamma\circ(h_1^{-1}\sigma)$ is $(E_1(a^{-1}K)\circ f_1^{-1}P(K))\circ\sigma_{Rg_{0,*}K}$, and the mate of $(\tau g_0^{-1})\circ\gamma'$ is $Rh_{1,*}(\tau_K)\circ Q(e_0^{-1}K)\circ x^{-1}E_0(K)$. Since mates are a well-defined assignment and the two transformations are equal by step 2, these two mates are equal. This is the displayed equality under the identifications $\sigma$ and $\tau$, for every $K$. The argument uses only units, counits and composition isomorphisms; no exchange map is cancelled or assumed invertible.

split_report.summary: Split the cube identity into three proof steps. The first expands the four exchanges as mates, the second compares the two inverse-image pastings using derived inverse-image coherence, and the third applies Mathlib mate-pasting and the mate bijection. No new node was needed; all supporting statements already exist.
split_report.blueprint: Sole blueprint proof paragraph of lem-kun-0ezt: the canonical-map comparison uses derived cube pasting. The three steps realize that cube-pasting comparison explicitly.

tool_uses.why: Generic coherence of derived inverse-image composition identifies the two canonical inverse-image pastings; the Kunneth unit has no replacement.
Generic mate-pasting is the categorical identity converting equality of pasted inverse-image comparisons into equality of exchange maps.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-eb7ac1e89 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four cited statements and the sources in full: Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 remark-base-change and Tag 0E47 remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, where the verification is omitted. The statement is true and well-typed. It needs only the six face equations, and no face has to be cartesian. Both sides agree once f_1^{-1}s^{-1} is identified with x^{-1}f_0^{-1} and y^{-1}e_0^{-1} with e_1^{-1}a^{-1}. Small cases checked: all comparison maps identities (P and Q become canonical identifications, so E_1=E_0), K=0, and the all-identity cube. The delivery creates no new nodes. My search for duplicates found none: sbc-lem-base-change-composition, sbc-lem-identity-and-base-change-composition and lem-kun-higher-exchange-coefficient-cube all state something different. Step 1: I checked the exchange orientations against def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange, namely (g_b,f_b,h_b,e_b) for E_b, (g_0,s,g_1,a) for P and (h_0,x,h_1,y) for Q. Step 3: clause 1 of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting gives each side as the mate of the pasted transformation gamma or gamma'. Fixed gap: gamma and gamma' have different source and target functors. Step 2 named only the target identification, and step 3 went from 'the mate assignment is a bijection' straight to equal mates. The proof also needs mates to be compatible with whiskering the side functors by sigma and tau, which follows from naturality of the unit for h_1 and naturality of tau against the counit for g_0. That is elementary from the explicit formula in def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, but it is not mate-pasting clause 3. The corrected item file in fixes/ rewrites steps 2 and 3 only: it defines sigma and tau, states gamma∘(h_1^{-1}sigma) = (tau g_0^{-1})∘gamma', and writes out the naturality argument. Statement, uses and proof_deps are unchanged. I accept the tool uses lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition (clause 3) and lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting.
